terms.gloss: set, go down (of the sun, the moon, the stars)
evidence: Catull. 5.4: sōlēs occidere et redīre possunt
Tac. Agr. 12.4: nec occidere et exsurgere
terms.comment: From cadō, with short i; not occīdō (long ī, from caedō), “kill”. The setting is occāsus (sunset).

phrases.english: suns can set and come back

phrases.latin: sōl nōn occidat super īrācundiam vestram
phrases.english: do not let the sun go down on your anger

phrases.latin: aspicī per noctem sōlis fulgōrem, nec occidere et exsurgere, sed trānsīre adfirmant
phrases.english: they say that the sun’s glow can be seen all night, and that it does not set and rise but passes across

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-catullus, loci-vulgata, loci-tacitus), checked against the editions named there.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 322.
